title: Introduction to the complement lecture
groupedBecause: This opening frames complement as an important but nomenclaturally challenging subject and sets expectations for the lecture.

title: Complement cascade fundamentals and the central role of C3
groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual and molecular framework for understanding how inactive complement becomes a pathogen-clearing response.

title: Complement activation pathways and the local activation threshold
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition generates enough surface-bound C3b to trigger complement activity.

title: Complement effector mechanisms
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement produces the effector responses that combat pathogens.

title: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activity to prevent damage to host cells.

title: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
groupedBecause: This subtopic connects the functions of complement components to the distinct clinical consequences of their deficiency.

title: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
groupedBecause: This subtopic examines pathogen adaptations that evade complement, extending the protein A example to its practical uses.

title: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the next lecture's subject.
